# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as ui from '../support/ui';

test.setTimeout(240_000);
test.describe("person timeline", () => {
  test("person timeline", { tag: '@functionality' }, async ({ browser }) => {
    const sheet = ui.sheetId();
    const pg_uma = await ui.userPage(browser, "uma", sheet);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-10");
    expect(await ui.setRate(pg_uma, {"grade": "A", "pct": "10.00"})).toBe(true);
    const p_ada = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Ada", "grade": "A"}));
    const c_ada_0 = ui.must(await ui.addClaim(pg_uma, p_ada, {"amount": "10.00", "date": "2026-03-01"}));
    const c_ada_1 = ui.must(await ui.addClaim(pg_uma, p_ada, {"amount": "20.00", "date": "2026-03-05"}));
    expect(await ui.claimAction(pg_uma, c_ada_0, "open")).toBe(true);
    const pg_vic = await ui.userPage(browser, "vic", sheet);
    expect(await ui.claimAction(pg_vic, c_ada_0, "settle")).toBe(true);
    await ui.refresh(pg_uma);
    expect(await ui.editPerson(pg_uma, p_ada, {"grade": "B", "gradeFrom": "2026-03-05"})).toBe(true);
    expect(await ui.hold(pg_uma, p_ada, {"from": "2026-03-02", "to": "2026-03-04"})).toBe(true);
    expect(await ui.retire(pg_uma, p_ada, "2026-03-08")).toBe(true);
    await ui.showRetired(pg_uma, true);
    await ui.refresh(pg_uma);
    await expect(pg_uma.getByTestId("person-row-" + p_ada).getByTestId("person-timeline-line")).toHaveText(["2026-03-01 claim 10.00 SETTLED", "2026-03-02 hold to 2026-03-04", "2026-03-05 grade B", "2026-03-05 claim 20.00 DRAFT", "2026-03-08 retired"]);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-12");
    expect(await ui.unretire(pg_uma, p_ada)).toBe(true);
    expect(await ui.hold(pg_uma, p_ada, {"from": "2026-03-05"})).toBe(true);
    await ui.refresh(pg_uma);
    await expect(pg_uma.getByTestId("person-row-" + p_ada).getByTestId("person-timeline-line")).toHaveText(["2026-03-01 claim 10.00 SETTLED", "2026-03-02 hold to 2026-03-04", "2026-03-05 grade B", "2026-03-05 claim 20.00 DRAFT", "2026-03-05 hold", "2026-03-08 retired", "2026-03-12 unretired"]);
    await ui.expectAudit(sheet, [
      `RATE_SET sheet=${sheet} by=uma grade=A rate=10.00`,
      `PERSON_ADDED sheet=${sheet} by=uma name=Ada grade=A`,
      `ROLLUP sheet=${sheet} by=uma person=Ada claimed=0.00 due-total=0.00 overdue-total=0.00`,
      `CLAIM_ADDED sheet=${sheet} by=uma person=Ada amount=10.00 date=2026-03-01`,
      `CLAIM_ADDED sheet=${sheet} by=uma person=Ada amount=20.00 date=2026-03-05`,
      `CLAIM_OPENED sheet=${sheet} by=uma person=Ada amount=10.00 date=2026-03-01`,
      `ROLLUP sheet=${sheet} by=uma person=Ada claimed=10.00 due-total=1.00 overdue-total=0.00`,
      `TOTALS sheet=${sheet} by=uma claimed-total=10.00 due-total=1.00 overdue-total=0.00`,
      `CLAIM_SETTLED sheet=${sheet} by=vic person=Ada amount=10.00 date=2026-03-01 number=FY2026-1 due=1.00`,
      `PERSON_EDITED sheet=${sheet} by=uma name=Ada grade=B`,
      `PERSON_HELD sheet=${sheet} by=uma name=Ada from=2026-03-02`,
      `PERSON_RETIRED sheet=${sheet} by=uma name=Ada from=2026-03-08`,
      `SNAPSHOT sheet=${sheet} by=uma name=Ada due-total=1.00`,
      `PERSON_UNRETIRED sheet=${sheet} by=uma name=Ada on=2026-03-12`,

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

-- A person can be retired from a date: they count as retired at once, whatever the date, and a claim
-- dated after it is refused. Null while the person is not retired.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN retired_from DATE;
-- A person can be put on hold: while held, their open claims count in no live total (settled ones still do).
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN held BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;
-- A person's grades, each recorded from a from-date (null = from the beginning of time: the first grade
-- the person was given). The grade in force on a date is the one with the latest from-date on or before
-- it; person.grade keeps only the first grade given.
CREATE TABLE person_grade (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    grade VARCHAR(1) NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE
);
CREATE INDEX person_grade_sheet ON person_grade (sheet_id, person_id);
INSERT INTO person_grade (sheet_id, person_id, grade, from_date) SELECT sheet_id, id, grade, NULL FROM person;
-- A person's holds, each from a from-date to an optional to-date (null: no end), both inclusive; a person may
-- have several over time. Only their open claims dated within a hold, and not bound by a statement, are left out
-- of the live totals. A person held before holds had dates is held from the beginning of time (null from-date).
CREATE TABLE person_hold (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    from_date DATE,
    to_date DATE
);
CREATE INDEX person_hold_sheet ON person_hold (sheet_id, person_id);
INSERT INTO person_hold (sheet_id, person_id, from_date, to_date) SELECT sheet_id, id, NULL, NULL FROM person WHERE held;
ALTER TABLE person DROP COLUMN held;
-- A retired person can be unretired: their retirement is kept as a past one, from its from-date to the sheet's today
-- when they were unretired. A claim dated after the from-date and before the to-date of a past retirement is refused.
CREATE TABLE person_retirement (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    from_date DATE NOT NULL,
    to_date DATE NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX person_retirement_sheet ON person_retirement (sheet_id, person_id);
-- The grades retired on the sheet: such a grade cannot be chosen for a person any more (those on it keep it).
CREATE TABLE grade_retired (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    grade VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, grade)
);
-- The sheet's today when the person was retired (null: from the beginning of time), so a pool's cuts taken as they
-- stood at the end of an earlier period count the person retired only when the retirement was made on or before it.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN retired_on DATE;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

# Refuse to run against a server that is not ours: an app left running on $PORT (an earlier
# bin/start that was never stopped, another sandbox) would take the tests and fail them all.
if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "bin/e2e: something is already serving on port ${PORT}; stop it (bin/stop) or set PORT to a free port" >&2
  exit 2
fi

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL. A loaded
# machine can take minutes to bring the JVM up; running the specs before it is ready fails every
# one of them for no reason, so wait long and fail loudly rather than run against nothing.
ready=0
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$ready" != 1 ]; then
  echo "bin/e2e: the app did not become healthy on port ${PORT} within 300s; see .run/app.log" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

- Each line has a `person-timeline-line` testid and reads `<date> grade X`, `<date> claim <amount> <status>`, `<date> hold` or `<date> hold to <date>`, `<date> retired`, or `<date> unretired`.
